response: Let me analyze this fixture. It's a status indicator dot component — a trivial difficulty case that primarily fails WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color). The plan should be concise, 1-2 pages, focused on the core issues: 1. Why color alone fails WCAG 1.4.1 2. Non-color alternative strategy 3. Contrast ratios per WCAG 1.4.11 4. Compact mode handling 5. No over-engineering (no keyboard interaction needed) Let me write a comprehensive but concise plan following the protocol structure, calibrated to this trivial component's risk level.# Status Indicator Dot Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, low vision users, color-blind users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS) **Feature:** A reusable `StatusDot` component displaying a colored dot indicating status (green/yellow/red) in sidebar navigation, table rows, and card headers. Optional compact mode hides text labels. **Risk Level:** Low — static visual indicator with no interaction; primary risk is WCAG 1.4.1 color-only communication failure. --- ## Scope & Context The `StatusDot` component currently ships as `` with zero accessibility attributes. It renders a small colored circle (CSS background or inline SVG) that is the **sole** visual indicator of status — no adjacent text label in compact mode, and even in full-label mode the dot itself carries no programmatic meaning. The core failure: **color alone communicates status**, which fails WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color for users with color vision deficiency (8% of men), low vision, or screen reader dependency. A red/green distinction is invisible to ~95% of deuteranopes. The dot must carry its semantic meaning programmatically so assistive technology can announce it independently of visual perception. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan ### Current Problem ```jsx // BROKEN: color-only communication, no programmatic status // renders ``` The dot is a presentational element with no semantic meaning. Screen readers announce nothing; sighted users rely entirely on color perception. ### Correct Structure (Full-Label Mode) When a text label accompanies the dot, the dot itself must be **hidden from assistive technology** to prevent double-announcement ("green circle Active"), and the visible text label provides the accessible name: ```jsx Active ``` - `aria-hidden="true"` on the dot per WCAG 1.1.1 — it is decorative when a sibling text label exists - The visible `.label` span provides the accessible name naturally (no ARIA needed) - No interactive wrapper; the status indicator is not focusable or actionable ### Correct Structure (Compact Mode) When only the dot shows, the semantic meaning must be embedded in the dot element itself: ```jsx ``` - `role="img"` + `aria-label` per WCAG 1.1.1 Non-Text Content — treats the colored dot as an image with a text alternative - The label describes **semantic status**, not visual appearance (e.g., "Active" not "green circle") - Screen readers announce: "Active, image" ### Status Label Mapping | Color Prop | Dot Background | Semantic Meaning | Accessible Text | WCAG 1.4.1 Justification | |------------|---------------|------------------|-----------------|--------------------------| | `green` | `#10b984` | Active / Online / Passing | "Active" | Red/green colorblind users cannot distinguish green from red without text | | `yellow` | `#eab308` | Warning / Pending / Degraded | "Warning" | Yellow may appear as pale or washed out to low-vision users | | `red` | `#ef4444` | Inactive / Offline / Failing | "Error" | Red is the most common colorblind-confusion pair with green | > **Product terminology note:** If the dashboard uses different status labels (e.g., "Passing"/"Failing" for deployments, "Online"/"Offline" for team members), the `aria-label` and visible label text must match the product's domain language. The component should accept a `label` prop or derive it from context rather than hardcoding generic terms. --- ## Interaction Pattern Design **The status dot is NOT an interactive widget.** It requires no keyboard interaction, no focus management, no APG pattern mapping beyond basic non-text content semantics. - No Tab stop (the dot does not receive focus) - No Enter/Space activation - No Escape behavior - No arrow key navigation If the surrounding list item or card is interactive (e.g., clicking a task row navigates to it), that interaction belongs on the parent element, not the dot. The dot remains `aria-hidden="true"` in full-label mode and `role="img" aria-label` in compact mode regardless of parent interactivity. --- ## Focus Management Plan **No focus management required.** The status dot is a static visual indicator: - It does not receive keyboard focus - It does not trap or redirect focus - It does not need focus restoration on close (it never opens) - If the parent list item/card is focusable, standard DOM order applies — the dot's `aria-hidden` ensures screen readers skip it and announce only the meaningful content --- ## State Communication Design The status dot has three static states. Each must be communicated programmatically: | State | Visual (Color) | Programmatic (Full-Label Mode) | Programmatic (Compact Mode) | WCAG Citation | |-------|----------------|--------------------------------|-------------------------------|---------------| | Active/Passing | Green `#10b984` | Visible text "Active" + `aria-hidden="true"` on dot | `role="img" aria-label="Active"` | 1.4.1, 1.1.1 | | Warning/Degraded | Yellow `#eab308` | Visible text "Warning" + `aria-hidden="true"` on dot | `role="img" aria-label="Warning"` | 1.4.1, 1.1.1 | | Error/Failing | Red `#ef4444` | Visible text "Error" + `aria-hidden="true"` on dot | `role="img" aria-label="Error"` | 1.4.1, 1.1.1 | **No dynamic state changes.** The status does not change in-place without a re-render that replaces the component. No live regions (`aria-live`) are needed — when the parent list/table updates with new data, standard DOM replacement handles the announcement through normal screen reader navigation. --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan ### WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color (Core Failure) > **Criterion:** "Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information" The current implementation uses color alone to indicate status. This fails for: - **Deuteranopia** (~6% of males): red and green appear nearly identical - **Protanopia** (~2% of males): same issue with red/green confusion - **Tritanopia** (<1%): blue/yellow confusion (less relevant here but still a risk) - **Low vision users**: reduced color saturation may make yellow indistinguishable from white background **Solution:** Every status must have a non-color indicator — either visible text label or programmatic `aria-label`. The dot's color becomes redundant confirmation, not the sole communication channel. ### WCAG 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast > **Criterion:** "The visual presentation of... graphics... is at least 3:1 against adjacent colors" The colored dot must maintain a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio against its immediate background: | Dot Color | Background | Ratio (approx) | Passes 1.4.11? | |-----------|------------|----------------|----------------| | Green `#10b984` on white `#ffffff` | ~2.5:1 | ❌ FAILS — needs darker green or lighter background | | Yellow `#eab308` on white `#ffffff` | ~1.8:1 | ❌ FAILS — yellow is notoriously low-contrast | | Red `#ef4444` on white `#ffffff` | ~3.2:1 | ✅ Passes (barely) | **Fix:** Adjust dot colors to meet 3:1 against the actual background color used in sidebar/table/card contexts. Recommended accessible values: | Status | Accessible Color | Contrast vs White | Contrast vs Gray `#f3f4f6` | |--------|------------------|-------------------|---------------------------| | Active (green) | `#059669` (emerald-700) | ~3.1:1 ✅ | ~2.8:1 ⚠️ borderline | | Warning (yellow) | `#d97706` (amber-700) | ~3.0:1 ✅ | ~2.7:1 ⚠️ borderline | | Error (red) | `#dc2626` (red-800) | ~4.5:1 ✅ | ~4.0:1 ✅ | > **Note:** If the dashboard uses a gray or dark background for table rows/sidebar, test dot-to-background contrast specifically — 1.4.11 requires 3:1 against adjacent colors, not just white. The `StatusDot` component must accept a `bgColor` prop or use CSS variables to compute contrast dynamically if backgrounds vary by context. ### WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing (if label is present) If the visible text label is shown alongside the dot, ensure: - Line height ≥ 1.5× font size - No fixed px heights that clip text at zoom - Label uses `rem` units for sizing ### Compact Mode Visual Strategy In compact mode where only dots show (no text labels), rely on **shape consistency** and **positioning**: - Dots are always the same shape (circle) — no shape-based distinction needed - Position is consistent (always left edge of list item/card header) - The programmatic `aria-label` carries the meaning; visual color provides redundant confirmation for sighted users --- ## Content Accessibility Plan ### Alt Text / Icon Labeling Strategy The status dot is an **icon-as-image** pattern. Per WCAG 1.1.1 Non-Text Content: - **Full-label mode:** The dot is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`). The visible text label ("Active", "Warning", "Error") provides the accessible name naturally — no `alt` or `aria-label` needed on the dot itself. - **Compact mode:** The dot carries semantic meaning via `role="img" aria-label=""`. This is equivalent to an `` pattern. ### Why NOT these alternatives: | Approach | Problem | WCAG Violation | |----------|---------|----------------| | `title` attribute on the dot | Tooltip only; not reliably announced by screen readers (NVDA reads it, VoiceOver often ignores it in browse mode) | 1.4.1 — unreliable non-color indicator | | `aria-label="green circle"` | Describes visual appearance, not semantic meaning | 1.1.1 — alt text must convey purpose, not decoration | | No label at all (color only) | Color-blind and screen reader users cannot determine status | 1.4.1 — color is sole indicator | ### Visually-Hidden Text Technique for Compact Mode If the team prefers visible-but-hidden text over `role="img" aria-label`, use the standard `.sr-only` pattern: ```css .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; } ``` ```jsx Active ``` This is functionally equivalent to `role="img" aria-label` but keeps the text in the DOM. Either approach satisfies WCAG — choose based on team preference and existing codebase patterns. The `aria-hidden="true"` + sibling visible label pattern (full-label mode) remains unchanged regardless of which compact-mode technique is chosen. --- ## Testing Strategy ### Automated Testing - **axe-core:** Verify no "color-only" violations, confirm `role="img"` elements have accessible names in compact mode, verify `aria-hidden` on decorative dots in full-label mode - **eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y (React):** Catch missing `alt`/`aria-label` on icon-like components at build time ### Manual Keyboard Testing - Tab through the page — status dots should NOT receive focus (they are not interactive) - Verify parent list items/cards that contain dots remain keyboard-accessible if they have their own interaction handlers - No Escape, Enter, or Space behavior expected on the dot itself ### Screen Reader Testing Scenarios 1. **Full-label mode:** Navigate to a task row → screen reader announces "Active" (from visible text), skips the decorative dot (`aria-hidden="true"`) — no double announcement like "green circle Active" 2. **Compact mode:** Navigate to a status-only element → screen reader announces "Active, image" (from `role="img" aria-label`) or just "Active" (if using `.sr-only` text) 3. **Status change simulation:** If the parent list re-renders with updated statuses, verify new status is announced on next navigation (no live region needed — standard DOM replacement handles this) ### Visual Regression Testing - **High-contrast Windows mode test:** Enable Windows High Contrast Mode → colored dots may render as default link color or be replaced entirely. Verify that in compact mode, the `aria-label` still conveys meaning even if visual colors disappear. In full-label mode, visible text labels ensure status is readable regardless of theme override. - **Color-blind simulation:** Use Chrome DevTools or Sim Daltonism to simulate deuteranopia → verify that without color perception, the non-color indicator (text label or aria-label) still communicates status correctly - **Zoom test at 200%:** Verify dot and label layout doesn't break; text labels remain readable ### Acceptance Criteria | Criterion | Pass Condition | WCAG | |-----------|----------------|------| | Color-only communication eliminated | Every status has a non-color indicator (visible text or aria-label) | 1.4.1 | | Dot contrast meets minimum | All dot colors ≥3:1 against their background in all contexts | 1.4.11 | | Decorative dots hidden from AT | `aria-hidden="true"` on dots that have sibling visible labels | 1.1.1 | | Compact mode has accessible name | Dots use `role="img" aria-label` or `.sr-only` text in compact mode | 1.1.1, 4.1.2 | | No double-announcement | Screen reader announces status once, not "green circle Active" | 1.3.1 | | High-contrast theme resilient | Status meaning survives Windows HC mode color overrides | 1.4.1, 1.4.11 | --- ## Implementation Tasks ### Task 1: Refactor `StatusDot` Component — Full-Label Mode 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `src/components/StatusDot.tsx` (modify) - `src/components/__tests__/StatusDot.test.tsx` (add tests) **Structure Stub:** ```jsx // Full-label mode: dot is decorative, sibling text provides meaning {label} ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `aria-hidden="true"` on the dot element (WCAG 1.1.1 Non-Text Content) — prevents double-announcement with sibling visible text **Props:** - `color: 'green' | 'yellow' | 'red'` — maps to accessible color values meeting 3:1 contrast - `label: string` — visible and programmatically-associated status text (e.g., "Active", "Warning", "Error") - No `aria-label`, no `role="img"` needed in this mode **Tests:** - Render with `color="green" label="Active"` → verify dot has `aria-hidden="true"`, label text is present and visible - Verify screen reader announces only "Active" (not "green circle Active") — use axe-core or manual NVDA/VoiceOver check - Verify no Tab focus on the dot element **WCAG Criteria:** 1.4.1 Use of Color, 1.1.1 Non-Text Content, 1.3.1 Info and Relationships --- ### Task 2: Implement Compact Mode — Dot as Accessible Image 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `src/components/StatusDot.tsx` (modify) - `src/components/__tests__/StatusDot.test.tsx` (add tests) **Structure Stub:** ```jsx // Compact mode: dot carries semantic meaning via role="img" + aria-label ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `role="img"` (WCAG 1.1.1) — establishes the dot as a non-text content element requiring an accessible name - `aria-label={label}` (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value) — provides the semantic status text ("Active", "Warning", "Error"), NOT visual description like "green circle" **Props:** - Same `color` and `label` props as Task 1 - A `compact: boolean` prop or context-based detection to switch between modes - In compact mode, no visible `.label` span is rendered — the dot itself carries the accessible name **Tests:** - Render with `color="red" label="Error" compact={true}` → verify `role="img"` and `aria-label="Error"` are present on the dot element - Verify screen reader announces "Error, image" (NVDA) or "Error" (VoiceOver) — not "red circle" - Verify no visible text is rendered in compact mode but accessible name is still available **WCAG Criteria:** 1.4.1 Use of Color, 1.1.1 Non-Text Content, 4.1.2 Name Role Value --- ### Task 3: Fix Dot Color Contrast Values 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `src/components/StatusDot.tsx` or `src/styles/status-dot.css` (modify color values) **Color Adjustments:** ```css /* Before — fails WCAG 1.4.11 on white background */ .dot--green { background-color: #10b984; } /* ~2.5:1 vs white ❌ */ .dot--yellow { background-color: #eab308; } /* ~1.8:1 vs white ❌ */ .dot--red { background-color: #ef4444; } /* ~3.2:1 vs white ✅ (barely) */ /* After — meets WCAG 1.4.11 ≥3:1 against white and common gray backgrounds */ .dot--green { background-color: #059669; } /* emerald-700, ~3.1:1 vs white ✅ */ .dot--yellow { background-color: #d97706; } /* amber-700, ~3.0:1 vs white ✅ */ .dot--red { background-color: #dc2626; } /* red-800, ~4.5:1 vs white ✅ */ ``` **Tests:** - Use axe-core or Chrome DevTools contrast checker to verify all three dot colors ≥3:1 against the actual backgrounds used in sidebar (`#ffffff` or `#f9fafb`), table rows (`#ffffff` or `#f3f4f6`), and card headers - Test with Windows High Contrast Mode enabled — dots may render as default link color; verify `aria-label`/`visible text` still conveys meaning **WCAG Criteria:** 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast, 1.4.1 Use of Color (color must not be sole indicator even if contrast passes) --- ## a11y-Critic Review Checkpoints | Checkpoint | After Task | Focus Areas | |-----------|-----------|------------| | 🔍 1 | Task 1 | Verify `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative dots in full-label mode prevents double-announcement; verify visible text label provides accessible name naturally without additional ARIA | | 🔍 2 | Task 2 | Verify compact-mode dots use `role="img" aria-label` with semantic status text (not "green circle"); verify no visible text leaks into DOM in compact mode but screen reader still announces the label | | 🔍 3 | Task 3 | Verify all dot colors meet ≥3:1 contrast against every background context where they appear; verify high-contrast Windows mode doesn't strip meaning when color is overridden | --- ## References -
